contentBlocks.title: How to Check Your SASSA Grant Status
contentBlocks.description: There are multiple ways to check your SASSA grant status — online via the SRD portal, through the WhatsApp line, by USSD code, or in person at a SASSA office. Find the method that works best for you.

secondaryCta.label: How to Apply for a Grant

contentBlocks.text: How to Check Your SASSA Grant Status

You can check your SASSA grant application or payment status using any of these methods. Pick whichever one fits you best — they all show the same information, so there is no right or wrong answer. The SRD online portal is the fastest and gives you the most detail, but if you have trouble with data or apps, the WhatsApp line or USSD code works just as well.

It is worth checking your status regularly, not just once. A grant that was approved can hit snags later — a bank verification that is suddenly flagged, a missed re-confirmation, or a review hold that needs your attention. Catching a problem early is a lot less stressful than discovering it on payment day, so a quick monthly check takes two minutes and saves you a lot of worry.

links.text: why your status might be on hold

contentBlocks.text: Can You Check with Just Your ID Number?

The short answer: on every channel, SASSA verifies you using your ID number plus the phone number you registered when you applied. You cannot check your status with the ID number alone. The portal, WhatsApp, USSD, and the call centre all pull up your file only when you provide both, because SASSA protects your records against identity fraud. If you have lost the phone number you applied with, update it first through the change-phone process, then any method below will work.

links.text: how to change the phone number on your SASSA application

contentBlocks.text: Method 1: Online Portal (Recommended)
Visit srd.sassa.gov.za. Enter your ID number and the phone number you used during application. You will receive an OTP via SMS to access your status dashboard.

Before you start, make sure the phone you enter is the one linked to your application. If you have changed your cell number since applying, the OTP will not reach you — sort that out first via the 'change phone number' process, otherwise you will be stuck in a loop of requests that never arrive.

links.text: how to change your SASSA phone number

contentBlocks.text: Method 2: SASSA WhatsApp Line
Save 082 046 8553 to your phone. Send 'SASSA' to start. Follow the prompts to check your balance, payment date, or application status. Free on most networks.

This method is handy if you are already on WhatsApp anyway. The chat menus walk you through step by step, and you do not need to remember any codes or web addresses. Just reply with the number of the option you want. One thing to remember: SASSA will never message you out of the blue asking for your PIN or OTP — always start the conversation yourself by sending 'SASSA'. The WhatsApp line has been updated before, so if 082 046 8553 stops responding, confirm the current number on sassa.gov.za rather than trusting a Google result.
Method 3: USSD Code

Dial *134*7737# on your mobile phone. Follow the menu to check your grant status. Standard network rates apply. You may also see *120*3210# or *120*69277# referenced online — USSD codes have changed over the years and vary between guides, so if one code does not work for you, try another or confirm the current code on sassa.gov.za.
Is There an Official SASSA Status App?

No. SASSA does not have an official status-checking app in the Play Store or App Store. There is no 'SASSA official app' on Android or iPhone — the official channels are the srd.sassa.gov.za portal, WhatsApp, USSD, the call centre, and SASSA offices. Apps that claim to be an official SASSA status checker are third-party tools at best and scams at worst. They are not connected to your grant records, and many ask for your ID and PIN, which you should never share.

The Moya app, a free South African messaging app, does offer a 'SASSA grants' section that lets you check your SRD status by entering your ID and phone number. Moya is a third-party app, not a SASSA product, and it retrieves the same records you can see yourself on the official portal. It can be useful if your regular data bundle is finished, but treat it like the portal and never enter more than your ID and registered phone number.

contentBlocks.title: There Is No Official SMS Status-Check Number
contentBlocks.text: SASSA sends you SMS updates, but it does not run a service where you text your ID number to a number to get a status back. Websites or social posts telling you to 'SMS your ID to 082 046 8553' or any other number are describing the WhatsApp line at best and scams at worst. Never text your ID number to an unverified number, and never reply to an SMS asking for your PIN or OTP.

USSD is the best backup option if your phone does not have data or an app at the moment. It works on any handset, even the simplest ones. Standard network rates apply, so it is not free like the WhatsApp line — but it is cheap and it gets the job done.
Method 4: Visit a SASSA Office
Bring your ID to any SASSA local office. A clerk can look up your status and provide a printout if needed.

If online checks are not working and you are near an office, this is a reliable fallback. Go early in the morning and bring your ID book or smart card. Some offices now have self-service kiosks where you can check your status on a touchscreen without queuing for a clerk — ask the staff at your nearest office if a kiosk is available there.

contentBlocks.title: Every Method Shows the Same Status
contentBlocks.text: The portal, WhatsApp, USSD, and the SASSA office all read from the same system. If one method shows 'Pending' and another shows something different, trust the newer result and give it a day or two — the systems sync up quickly.
Frequently Asked Questions

faqs.question: Is there an official SASSA status app?
faqs.answer: No. SASSA has no official app in the Play Store or App Store. Apps advertising a 'SASSA official status check' are third-party or fraudulent — the only official channels are the srd.sassa.gov.za portal, WhatsApp, USSD, the 0800 60 10 11 call centre, and SASSA offices. Never enter your PIN into any app claiming to be SASSA.

faqs.question: Can I check my SASSA status with only my ID number?
faqs.answer: No — every channel needs your ID number plus the phone number you registered when you applied. SASSA matches both to pull up your file, to stop strangers from viewing your records. If you lost the phone number you applied with, update it first via the change-phone process, then check again.

faqs.question: Why is my status still showing 'Pending' after weeks?
faqs.answer: 'Pending' means your application is still being checked and no decision has been made yet. It can stay on Pending for a while during busy periods, especially around re-confirmation. Keep checking, and if it has been more than 90 days, contact SASSA on 0800 60 10 11 to ask for an update.

faqs.question: I keep getting an error when I try to log into the SRD portal. What now?
faqs.answer: Try the other methods — the WhatsApp line (082 046 8553) or USSD *134*7737#. If those also fail, you can visit a SASSA office or call 0800 60 10 11. Portal login errors are often temporary, so clearing your browser cache and trying again after a while also helps.

faqs.question: Do I need data to check my status on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: The SASSA WhatsApp line is free on most networks, including on a zero-data plan from the main providers. If you are worried about data, the USSD code *134*7737# is another option that works on any phone, though standard rates may apply.

faqs.question: Can someone check my status on my behalf?
faqs.answer: Only your ID number and linked phone number are needed on the portal, so a family member with those details can log in for you. If you allow a helper to use a kiosk or ask a SASSA clerk on your behalf, never share your OTP — and be very careful who you trust with your ID and phone number.
